label: prop:golden-skew-dual-node
title: Skew-dual golden node at $q = \varphi^2$ under the bar involution $q \leftrightarrow q^{-1}$
html:
The Hecke bar involution \sigma \leftrightarrow \sigma^{-1} acts on the substrate parameter as q \leftrightarrow q^{-1}. In terms of s = \sqrt{q}, this is s \leftrightarrow 1/s. This involution maps the golden-ratio node q_{\mathrm{gold}} = 1/\varphi^2 (golden-ratio degeneration) to the skew-dual golden node:

  q^{*}_{\mathrm{gold}}
  =  \varphi^2
  =  \frac{3 + \sqrt{5}}{2}
   \approx  2.618.

The minimal polynomial of 1/\varphi over \mathbb{Q} is s^2 + s - 1. Applying s \mapsto 1/s and clearing denominators yields the bar-involute:

  s^2 - s - 1.

This is the minimal polynomial of \varphi. The involution s \leftrightarrow 1/s exchanges these quadratics up to sign. Their roots form the bar-paired set \{1/\varphi, \varphi\} on the positive real axis.
